# Every US dollar sold in August, and the same number bought straight back.
#
# Imported onto `a_cad_book_that_bought_usd_before_selling_and_rebuying_it.txt`
# with `{usd_basis}` replaced by the guid of the cost basis its 2026-01-10
# purchase opened. A guid is minted fresh on each import, so it is read from
# `fx-balances` and substituted before this file is imported.
#
# - 2026-08-01  1,000.00 USD sold at 1.50. Valued at what those dollars cost
#               — 1,300.00 CAD — against the 1,500.00 the sale fetched, so
#               `$residual$` books a 200.00 CAD gain and the January cost
#               basis falls to nothing.
# - 2026-08-01  1,000.00 USD bought again at 1.50, opening a second cost basis
#               of 1,000.00 USD at 1,500.00 CAD.
#
# What the pair is for: the book holds 1,000.00 USD both before and after, and
# a cost basis balance of 1,000.00 USD both before and after — but the cost
# behind it changes from 1,300.00 to 1,500.00 on 2026-08-01.
#
# A sheet drawn as of 2026-06-30 therefore has a correct answer of 50.00 CAD:
# on that date the book held the January dollars, worth 1,350.00 at the 06-30
# price of 1.35 against 1,300.00 of cost. Reading the cost bases as they stand
# at the end of the book instead gives 1,350.00 against 1,500.00 — a loss of
# 150.00 — because the quantities match while the costs do not, so nothing
# refuses it and the sheet balances on a figure that is wrong by 200.00.
2026-08-01 * "Sell 1,000.00 USD at 1.50"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank -1000.00 USD
		share_price: "1.30"
		value: "-1300.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{usd_basis}"
	Assets:CAD Bank 1500.00 CAD
	Income:FX Gain $residual$ CAD

2026-08-01 * "Buy 1,000.00 USD at 1.50"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank 1000.00 USD
		share_price: "1.50"
		value: "1500.00"
	Assets:CAD Bank -1500.00 CAD
